part.text: The bug is in `fixedpoint_d2string` in src/util.c:650. For values like `0.0001` (integer part is 0 and the scaled value has few digits), the zero-fill loop `for (i = integer_digits + 1; i < fractional_digits; i++)` stops before filling all fractional positions, leaving uninitialized bytes in the output buffer.
Now let me verify the fix with a quick standalone test:

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `fixedpoint_d2string` (src/util.c:725), introduced by the 7.0.6 formatting change used by `addReplyDoubleDistance` for GEORADIUS/GEODIST/`WITHDIST` replies.

- The zero-fill loop stopped at `fractional_digits` instead of `size - 1`, so when the scaled value had fewer digits than the fraction width (e.g. distance `0.0001` scaled to `1`), trailing fractional bytes in the stack buffer were left uninitialized — producing mangled replies like `0.00\xfc1`.
- Verified the fix with a standalone C harness (all boundary cases: `0.0001`, `-0.0001`, `0.00001`, `9.8182`, `100.0`, etc.), then ran the full `unit/geo` suite in the eval container — all tests pass, including `GEOSEARCH with small distance` which asserts `{1 0.0001}`.
- Also ran `unit/introspection-2` and `unit/type/zset` — no regressions.
